name: Dolphin
description: Constructs 3D acoustic holograms at 120 kHz resolving object density, shape, and internal structure. Unihemispheric sleep: one brain half rests while other navigates. Signature whistles function as names. Cooperative bubble-net hunting.

core_attributes.neurology: unihemispheric sleep, spindle neurons, echolocation cortex
core_attributes.pattern: acoustic holography, cultural play, cooperative hunting, signature identity

scope.definition: Angular resolution of dolphin biosonar target discrimination at 10 m range, expressed as fraction of objects distinguishable by shape alone (excluding size/material cues), in controlled tank experiments.

evidence.source: Au (1993) 'The Sonar of Dolphins', Springer; Nachtigall & Moore eds. (1988) 'Animal Sonar', Plenum; Herman et al. (1998) echolocation shape discrimination studies.
cross_domain_examples: bottlenose dolphin discriminates cylinders differing by 2 mm wall thickness at 10 m
fin shape discrimination accuracy 0.95 at 3 m, 0.88 at 10 m (Au 1993)
bat biosonar angular resolution 1-3 degrees (convergent echolocation evolution)
submarine sonar: 0.92 angular discrimination at equivalent frequency/range tradeoff

scope.falsifiability: If dolphin echolocation resolution is shown to fall below 0.70 in controlled shape-discrimination tasks at standardized 10 m range, the holographic reconstruction model is oversimplified.
scope.measurement_limits: Resolution degrades with range, background reverberation, and target complexity. Values reflect ideal tank conditions; open ocean performance is 0.80-0.88 due to multipath.

scope.definition: Fraction of sleep time during which one cerebral hemisphere maintains waking-level vigilance (EEG amplitude >50% of awake baseline), averaged across bottlenose dolphin studies in captivity and wild populations.

evidence.source: Lyamin et al. (2008) 'Cetacean sleep: an unusual form of mammalian sleep', Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 32:1451-1484; Mukhametov (1984) 'Sleep in marine mammals', Experimental Brain Research suppl.
cross_domain_examples: EEG recordings confirm unihemispheric slow-wave sleep in bottlenose dolphins
beluga whales maintain 0.96 unihemispheric alertness during sleep
migratory birds perform unihemispheric sleep during long flights (convergent evolution)

scope.falsifiability: If EEG studies consistently show both dolphin hemispheres entering slow-wave sleep simultaneously for >10% of total sleep time, the strict unihemispheric model fails.
scope.measurement_limits: True bilateral sleep is occasionally observed in captive dolphins in very safe environments. Unihemispheric fraction varies with perceived predation risk.

scope.definition: Capture success rate per herding event when ≥3 dolphins perform synchronized mud-ring, carousel, or strand-feeding tactics, compared to 0.40 for opportunistic solo foraging on schooling fish.

evidence.source: Gazda et al. (2005) 'A division of labour with role specialization in group-hunting bottlenose dolphins', Proceedings Royal Society B 272:135-140; Smolker & Pepper (1999) behavioural ecology of cooperative foraging.
cross_domain_examples: strand-feeding dolphins: 0.91 capture success vs 0.35 solo pursuit (Smolker 1999)
mud-ring cooperative herding: 0.88 success in Sarasota Bay population
lion pride cooperative ambush: analogous role-division hunting strategy 0.30 success rate
wolf pack relay chase: convergent cooperative capture strategy in mammalian carnivores

scope.falsifiability: If cooperative dolphin groups show no statistically higher per-individual caloric return than solo foragers over 200+ hunts, the cooperative advantage is energetically neutral.
scope.measurement_limits: Success rates are strongly context-dependent: prey schooling density, water depth, and group experience matter. Mud-ring technique is culturally transmitted in specific populations only.
